title: S4 counting is #P-hard on closed manifolds with first homology Z/2
claim: Target: for a knot K in S3 let T(K) be the number of homomorphisms from the knot group to S4 sending the meridian to a transposition, and C_p(K) = |Hom(pi1 S3_p(K), S4)| for integral p-surgery along the preferred longitude, whose group is the knot group modulo mu^p lambda and whose first homology is Z/p. Splitting by the class of the meridian image, C_2 = 4 + T + F_(c^2) and C_4 = 4 + T + F_1, where F_e counts 4-cycle colourings with longitude e: transposition longitudes are trivial and transposition and 4-cycle colourings are equinumerous (CLOSED-H1-20261025-001B), double transpositions give 3 abelian maps and 3-cycles never survive. Hence for every knot C_2(K) + C_4(K) = 8 + 3 T(K), and, using that the longitude of a connected sum is the product of the longitudes and the trefoil's fixed-meridian numbers (5 transposition lifts; 4-cycle lifts: 1 with trivial longitude, 4 with longitude c^2), 3 C_2(K) + C_2(K # trefoil) = 16 + 12 T(K). With BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A, counting homomorphisms to S4 is #P-hard under Turing reductions, with two queries per knot, for closed orientable 3-manifolds with first homology Z/2 given by integral surgery on knot diagrams; abelian-by-nilpotent targets, including all metabelian groups, are polynomial there (BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001B).
failure_conditions: A knot on which C_2 + C_4 differs from 8 + 3T, or 3 C_2(K) + C_2(K # trefoil) differs from 16 + 12T.
A closed count whose split by meridian class differs from 1 + 3 + T + (4-cycle terms), or a 3-cycle term that survives p = 2 or 4.
A surgered manifold whose first homology is not Z/p, or a convention test (S3_2 of the trefoil: 58; S3_6: 90) that fails.
A control that cannot fail: dropping the 4-cycle terms, using the blackboard longitude, or a virtual knot must break the identities.
foundation_claim_scope: Closed orientable 3-manifolds given by integral surgery on knot diagrams, with first homology Z/2 (and Z/4 for the first identity); counting homomorphisms to S4; Turing reductions with two queries per knot on top of the reduction of BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A. Cited, not proved: the longitude of a connected sum, conversion of surgery diagrams to triangulations, and what CLOSED-H1-20261025-001B and BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A cite. Other solvable groups such as SL(2,3) and GL(2,3) are not covered. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof (cited: the longitude of a connected sum, conversion of surgery diagrams to triangulations, and the inputs CLOSED-H1-20261025-001B and BOUNDED-H1-20261025-001A); check.py (standard library, under 1 s) computes every closed count by brute force over all S4 homomorphisms of the knot group kept when rho(mu)^p rho(lambda) = 1: convention tests (S3_2 of the trefoil 58 = Hom(binary octahedral, S4); S3_-2 58; S3_6 90 = L(2,1) # L(3,2); S3_1 1; first homology Z/p by Smith normal form, Z for p = 0), the meridian-class bookkeeping 1 + 3 + T + 4-cycle terms with no 3-cycle term, the trefoil fixed-meridian numbers (5; 1, 4), and both identities on 13 knots including tripled alternating diagrams, a gadget knot and a connected sum; controls: dropping the 4-cycle terms, the blackboard longitude and a virtual knot each break the identity. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive finite checks
